about: Amendments that carry out docs/decisions/2026-10-30-diffract-verb-and-imf-abbreviation.md, [USER]'s two decisions of 2026-10-30. Applied on top of amendments-2026-10-29.json (give both to tools/ai-review/compile-ruling-set.js, that file first). The verb gets its own ruling, listing the three English forms the word-bounded matcher needs (diffract also reaches diffracts; diffraction, diffractometer and the noun ruling are untouched). The abbreviation becomes three English forms of the existing intermolecular-force ruling: IMF and IMFs both, since a headword of 3 characters or fewer is matched case-sensitively with no plural, and the spaced alt-text form I M F, which also reaches the spaced plural I M F s (ch10 m68770). Hand-written input: its sha256 is recorded in the compiled artifact, so any edit must be followed by a recompile.

amendments.decision: Decision 1: the verb and the participle follow the noun, diffract → beygja / beygjast, diffracted → beygður; the target is the infinitive, whose stem beyg- every one of those forms carries
Decision 2: the abbreviation is an English form of the ruling, IMF, IMFs and the spaced alt-text form I M F count as uses of intermolecular force → millisameindakraftur
